name: Marcy Abong
title: Special memories of Paul throughout the years; with love from Marcy.
body:
Hi Oli! 😄 I cannot wait for you to read all of these wonderful memories about your Dad, Paul, from everyone who cared for him. I know you will have heard this countless times, but I must say again, he loved you so much. I have known your aunt Hanna since we were in middle school, and I am lucky to have spent a lot of time with your family over the years. Paul was the quintessential "big brother"; always there to help with any issue (mechanical or otherwise), and there to give a skeptical and all-knowing look when we were being goofy teenagers running around the village 😅 
One of my earliest memories of Paul was from Hanna's 12th (or 13th) birthday party sleepover at the house. We had a dance party in the dining room, and our DJ was none other than Pauly D. We all had so much fun, and it was the first of many good times to come at your house over the years. 
Another great tradition was the holiday open houses your grandmother Gunna would host. One year, after the main festivities had ended, me, Hanna, Anika, and Paul were together watching old family home movies downstairs. Paul had the biggest smile watching footage of himself as a child with his Dad, your grandfather, Michael. We all shared a good laugh that day. 
Another favorite memory of Paul is one that I shared with Hanna recently. We were in our early 20s, and your aunt had started to spend more time in Iceland, transitioning to living there fulltime. I had visited her many times over the years, and on this occasion we were flying together from Boston. Your Dad was giving us a ride to the airport, in one of his classic Volvos, and he played us The Low End Theory by A Tribe Called Quest on cassette. From the first note, I was hooked. It is one of those musical moments that stays with you, and will always come back to when I listen to it now. He let us take the tape with us, and we listened to it many times on that trip. 
The last time I saw Paul was for Christmas in 2024. I stopped by the house to visit with Hanna. I came in the back door into the kitchen, and there he was cooking, holding you. We took you into your playpen and played with your toys. When you started to cry,  he came over and told us to give you a hug! 😊 It was so clear that being a father came naturally to him, effortless. I feel grateful to have seen the two of you together, it always hold a special place in my heart. You are so loved by so many people. If you ever need anything, know that I am here for you as an extension aunt. 
All of my love,
Marcy 💕💖💛🧡
